title: Archive soft-deleted rows and implement TTL compaction pipeline for control plane
creator: Priya Nair
description: Background: The control plane Postgres clusters have accumulated a large volume of soft-deleted/tombstoned rows in several high-cardinality tables (projects, project_memberships, audit_events). This increases table size, slows full-table scans and aggregate queries, and magnifies bloat that VACUUM/VACUUM FULL struggles to reclaim during peak traffic. Goal: introduce a safe, operational archiving and TTL compaction pipeline to remove/compact soft-deleted rows older than the retention window, archive the data as compressed parquet to object storage for legal/forensics, and maintain a read-only historical store for occasional queries. This will reduce on-disk size and improve query latency for hot control-plane paths without losing retainment guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Configurable per-table retention policy (default 90 days) exposed in console/config repo
Background compaction worker running with rate-limiting and backpressure to avoid replica lag
Archived data stored in S3 as partitioned, compressed Parquet with schema snapshot and manifest
Post-archive table size reduced by at least 35% on average for targeted tables in the staging cluster
No production query regressions (99th percentile latency for control-plane read SLOs remains within baseline + 5%)
A documented rollback and rehydration process exists and is tested on staging
tasks: Audit and enumerate all tables with soft-delete patterns and estimate row volumes
Define retention defaults and per-customer override policy with legal/compliance
Prototype archival format and small-scale backfill in staging (parquet + gzip + schema manifest)
Build compaction worker service (k8s job) with pause/resume and concurrency limits
Integrate object-store lifecycle and encryption (SSE + KMS) and test access controls
Implement read-path for historical queries via fdw/sync or an on-demand rehydrate lambda
Add observability: compaction throughput, bytes archived, replica lag, delete/fail counters
Run canary on low-traffic tenant set for one week and capture performance telemetry
Schedule broad rollout with monitoring and runbook for operator intervention
migration_plan: 1) Create archive schema and manifest table in control plane (staging). 2) Run dry-run exporter for 1% sample of soft-deleted rows and validate parquet schema. 3) Deploy compaction worker to staging targeting noncritical tenants; verify object uploads and manifests. 4) Execute controlled background compaction in production on a small tenant cohort for 72 hours; monitor replica lag and application errors. 5) Gradually widen cohort (10% -> 50% -> 100%) while tuning rate limits. 6) After full rollout, schedule periodic compaction sweeps and set TTL automation to mark candidates older than retention for immediate archive. Note: all steps use rate limiting and safe guards to abort on sustained replica lag > 30s or error spikes.
rollback_plan: If we see sustained regressions or data loss risk: 1) Immediately pause compaction workers via k8s rollout and feature flag. 2) Use manifests to confirm archived object integrity. 3) Rehydrate affected partitions from S3 into a hot rehydrate table (tested on staging) using streaming copy; reintroduce rows to primary tables under a maintenance window. 4) Run consistency checks and re-run any failed transactions via stored manifests. All operator steps will be in the runbook and exercised in a dry-run before full production rollout.
